plan.contextChunk: This figure is an annotated graph of one full cycle of a transformed sine wave, marked up to expose its midline, amplitude, and period. The vertical y-axis carries ticks from -2 up to 4, the horizontal x-axis is labeled at pi/2 and at pi, and both axes end in arrowheads. The solid dark blue curve leaves the y-axis at height 1, rises to a maximum of 4 a quarter of the way along, falls back through that starting height, bottoms out at -2 near three-quarters of the way, and returns to height 1 at pi. A horizontal orange arrow at the level y = 1 extends rightward from the vertical axis, labeled Midline: y = 1. A vertical teal arrow runs up the curve's peak from that orange level to the maximum, tagged by a leader with Amplitude: |A| = 3. Below the plot, a red double-headed arrow spans the width of the drawn cycle beneath the label Period = pi. The three annotations measure independent things: the vertical center of the oscillation, the stretch away from that center, and the horizontal distance before the shape repeats. Taken together they are the quantities needed to reconstruct the equation of a sinusoid from its picture alone.

interactionPlan.concept: Amplitude, midline, and period describe three independent features of a sinusoid: vertical distance from center, vertical shift of the center line, and horizontal repeat length.

interactions.label: Amplitude |A|
interactions.teaches: Amplitude is the vertical distance from the midline to a peak or trough, not the total height of the graph

interactions.label: Midline y = D
interactions.teaches: The midline is the sinusoid's vertical center; moving it shifts the entire wave up or down without changing the wave's amplitude

interactions.label: Period P
interactions.teaches: The period is the horizontal distance required for one complete cycle, independent of the wave's height or vertical position

demo_steps.title: Read the original graph
demo_steps.narration: The curve oscillates around the orange midline y = 1. Its peak is 3 units above that line, and one full cycle is completed over a horizontal distance of pi.

demo_steps.title: Change amplitude only
demo_steps.narration: Increasing or decreasing amplitude moves the peak and trough farther from or closer to the midline. The orange midline stays fixed, so the vertical stretch is isolated.

demo_steps.title: Move the midline
demo_steps.narration: Changing the midline shifts the entire sine wave up or down. The distance from the midline to the peak remains the amplitude.

demo_steps.title: Stretch the period
demo_steps.narration: Changing the period stretches or compresses the wave horizontally. The graph still completes exactly one full cycle over the red span.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: A sinusoid's equation can be reconstructed by separating vertical center, vertical distance from that center, and horizontal repeat length.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Use a clean coordinate-plane style with black axes and arrowheads, a thick dark blue sine curve, orange for the midline annotation, teal for the amplitude annotation, and red for the period annotation. In the default view, show one cycle beginning at x = 0 on y = 1, peaking near x = pi/4 at y = 4, crossing the midline near x = pi/2, reaching a trough near x = 3pi/4 at y = -2, and returning to y = 1 at x = pi. Slider changes should dynamically update the curve, the colored measurement arrows, and the text labels so they always report the current amplitude, midline, and period. When period changes, relabel the midpoint tick as P/2 and the endpoint tick as P, while preserving pi/2 and pi formatting in the default state.

Inspecting the graph, we can determine that the period is π, the midline is y=1, and the amplitude is 3. See the figure.

A graph of y=3sin(2x)+1. The graph has an amplitude of 3. There is a midline at y=1. There is a period of pi. Local maximum at (pi/4, 4) and local minimum at (3pi/4, -2).
